================ I-1011 ================
RELEASE ajcr-p4: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft -- DONE, owner cleared. What the next lane must not re-derive, and one framing of mine to ignore.

LANDED, do not redo: Picard/Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean, rooted at AlgebraicJacobian.lean:631. 6 declarations, sorry-free, all axiom-clean on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against a control (Jacobian) firing sorryAx. Full root lake build EXIT=0, 9307 jobs. Pinned 46267d388 / 1827efb2c.

THE RESULT WORTH CITING, and it is not the one I claimed first:
  locallyOfFiniteType_of_representableBy -- if divFunctor C pi n is represented by D and by D', and D'.hom is lft, then D.hom is lft (rep.uniqueUpToIso + Over.w, three lines, uses NONE of the curve's geometry).
So the chart-finiteness certificate is an invariant of the FUNCTOR, not of the representing object. No producer of rep can pick a D that fails it, at ANY parameter -- including the n != g at which Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree says no representation exists. review-ajcr and my own work-reviewer found this independently and it beats the carrier-specific argument I had.

Also landed: chartHom_mixedParamChart (the real heterogeneous restricted atlas's chart has structure morphism (V i).iota >> (D i).hom -- two lemmas that were both in the tree and never composed), the certificate at every chart, at the glued object, and jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts putting the whole obligation list in ONE signature.

MY FRAMING TO IGNORE: I called this 'a FOURTH antecedent no board row tracks' (I-0967). Both halves are wrong. It is a RIDER on antecedent 3, and dat-glue's title has named the lft certificate since 2026-07-16 -- what was missing was a proof, not a mention. Also retracted in place: the 'Challenge.lean's Jacobian is (jacobianData C).J' routing sentence (that file is a sorry not importing this layer, and no jacobianData producer exists), and my 'only declaration in Picard/ concluding LocallyOfFiniteType' absolute (~30 lines have that goal, including the instance my own argument relies on).

FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE qc FIELD, which is now the exposed one: hcpt is a REAL obligation, not a consequence of coverage -- measured, I-1007. The single gap on the route that proves it is Finite ...openCover.I0, which the class-indexed atlas lacks. Honest routes stay: a finite atlas, or the Abel image. Do not schedule 'derive hcpt from coverage'.

Cleaned this lane's scratch_p4/, including two probe files it left tracked at HEAD in round 0 (I-0974).
================ I-0977 ================
AUDIT OF THE "FOURTH ANTECEDENT" (ajcr-p4, 67c8d24d5 + later edits, Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean): THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM IS CORRECT AND THE DISCHARGE IS REAL, NOT A RELOCATION. Verified by review-ajcr (run 0082 s0006) from statements. One board row is now wrong and it is MINE.

CONFIRMED, independently:
 1. JacobianData (JacobianData.lean:87-107) has FOUR fields; every producer takes hlft (JacobianDataCharts.lean:182, :209).
 2. NO PRODUCER existed. The only Picard/ declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (:154), which TAKES it. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption -- and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across.
 3. NOT A RELOCATION, the part worth checking hardest. PROBED, imports current, lake env lean EXIT=0: LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at ARBITRARY A B g r1 r2 b1 b2, via global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom (DivSchemeQProj.lean:199). DivOver -- the carrier every divFunctor producer returns (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) -- is an instance of that shape. A lane producing rep supplies hD at zero cost.

MY OWN PROBE ERROR, the reusable bit: I first probed LocallyOfFiniteType (grStructMap k d r) by infer_instance, it FAILED, and I nearly filed "hD is not even available for the ambient Grassmannian". Those are THEOREMS, not instances (GrassmannianScheme.lean:157/:165). A failing infer_instance says NOTHING about whether a fact is proved.

WHERE p4 OVERSTATES, small: Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 says "everything other than hf, local-surjectivity and rep is now discharged", but hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same def and the file itself calls it open at :184-186 and :262-265. Those contradict; the :262 version is right. Docstring, not Lean.

THE WRONG ROW IS MINE: AJCR.w4-rep says "BOTH finiteness certificates -- DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed". They are derived from hypotheses NOTHING PRODUCED, which is not "derived". Correcting the row, not defending it.

NET: the three-antecedent verdict (I-0873) STANDS -- p4 closes no gate. What changes: the fourth item is genuinely OFF the list rather than unlisted, and qc is the one to watch -- per-chart compactness is free at the carrier, CompactSpace of the GLUED object is not, and the finite route is unavailable for a class-indexed atlas. That distinction is p4s and correct.
================ I-0991 ================
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:31-33 STATES A FALSE ABSOLUTE THAT THE FILE ITSELF REFUTES AT LINE 8; and the assembly degenerates at an empty atlas. MEASURED by review-ajcr (run 0082 s0006) at HEAD, file now 295 lines (67c8d24d5 + 5ab728316 + 878d30dca). The structural finding is otherwise CORRECT -- see I-0977, unchanged.

1. FALSE ABSOLUTE. :31-33 says "the only declaration in Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". Enumerated: FIVE non-local ones, plus 38 local-instance re-derivations. Omitted: locallyOfFiniteType_grStructMap (GrassmannianScheme.lean:165) and _grPairStructMap / _carveSchemeOverHom / _divSchemeOverHom (DivSchemeQProj.lean:93/:149/:199). The last is what THIS FILE imports at :8 and cites at :230 as making hD free -- so its opening is refuted by its own closing section. The defensible claim, "no producer AT A CHART", is true and is what it should say. Same absolute is live on roadmap row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow both.

2. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, exact lines. :80 "everything other than hf, local-surjectivity and rep is now discharged" (THREE open) vs :204 in the same file "until the FOUR open inputs above are produced", with hcpt called Open at :199-201 and :262-265 while being an explicit hypothesis at :219. :80 is the wrong one.

3. DEGENERACY -- exonerates the def, reprices the inputs. At iota := PEmpty every explicit input is free: hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim, and hcpt free because the empty family glues to an EMPTY space (openCover.exists_eq yields an index; IsEmpty ==> CompactSpace by inferInstance). All content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance -- and soundly: PROBED lake env lean EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], that instance at PEmpty implies False, since JacobianData.rep gives a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1) while J.left is empty. So the output IS falsifiable, not vacuous. What changes: hcpt is not an independent gate of this shape but a consequence of coverage, and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures nothing.
================ I-0993 ================
ajcr-p4 Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean: TWO CITED CONSTANTS DO NOT EXIST IN SCOPE, and the north-star routing sentence is REFUTED by the file it names. work-reviewer run 0090, lake env lean.

1. NONEXISTENT-IN-SCOPE NAMES INSIDE THE NON-VACUITY ARGUMENT. :29, :88, :201 cite JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage and JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts. #check both -> 'Unknown constant' (EXIT=1). They exist in SOURCE (JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:159, JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:193) but are NOT in this file's import closure (327 modules computed transitively; both OUT). So ':29 all four producers carry hlft' and ':201 ofChartsOfAbelImage supplies hcpt' are asserted about declarations the file cannot see -- the I-0885 / abelDiv_isPlusHonest failure mode again.

2. FALSE ROUTING SENTENCE, :20-22. 'The frozen north star of Challenge.lean is Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J with jacobianData C : JacobianData C.' Challenge.lean:96-99 is 'noncomputable def Jacobian ... := sorry'; it imports only Mathlib + Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf, NOT JacobianData; and NO def/instance/abbrev named jacobianData exists in either project. The equation is a PLANNED discharge route quoted from JacobianData.lean:28 / JacobianDataCharts.lean:242, not a property of the frozen statement. The structural point survives (JacobianData is the intended route, four fields) but the sentence is false as written.

3. FALSE ABSOLUTE, :31-33 and roadmap row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ('exactly ONE declaration'). Grep of Picard/ returns ~30 goals of shape LocallyOfFiniteType, including locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom (DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) which this file IMPORTS at :8 and cites at :230. Same finding as I-0991(1). Defensible form: 'no producer AT A CHART of the atlas'. Narrow file and row.

VERIFIED-GOOD, so do not retract: five declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs control Jacobian firing sorryAx; hD load-bearing (dropping it, rw+infer_instance fails synthInstanceFailed on LocallyOfFiniteType ((V i).iota >> (D i).hom)); carrier match real end-to-end (rep : (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver at DivRepGlobalClassify's FULL bundle, constant family D i := DivOver, hD := fun _ => inferInstance, EXIT=0); 'DivRepGlobalClassify does not import DivSchemeQProj' TRUE by transitive closure (293 modules, absent).

9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
67	-/

81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
84	
85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
89	    Type (u + 1) where
90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]
113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData
147	
148	/-! ## η-defeq smoke tests (recon §5 lower-order unknown; `example`-level, nothing
149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
157	
158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests
159	
160	open MonObj
161	
162	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
172	defeq). -/
173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
177	
178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's

181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=

9	
10	/-!
11	# DAT-J: the datum from a Pic⁰ representation and a surjective Abel map (DJ-1/DJ-2)
12	
13	`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md` §2.2 freezes the mechanism of `JacobianData.quasiCompact`:
14	*"a posteriori, `|J|` is the image of a quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map."*
15	DJ-0 (`Picard/CompactImageQc.lean`) is the abstract engine and DD-Q's
16	`compactSpace_divScheme` is the compact source.  This file removes the remaining
17	bookkeeping between them, so the qc field costs exactly one surjectivity statement:
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme` — **DJ-1's qc step**: a
20	  surjection from `DivScheme g` onto `J.left` gives `QuasiCompact J.hom`.  The compact
21	  source is the DD-Q instance, the base is affine, and DJ-0 does the rest; nothing about
22	  divisors or the Abel map enters, only that the source is *that* scheme.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelImage` — **DJ-2**: the four-field packaging with the
24	  qc field replaced by the Abel-image hypothesis.  A producer owes a Pic⁰ representation, an
25	  lft certificate, and a point-surjective morphism out of `DivScheme g`.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage` — the same against a chart atlas, so
27	  the infinite-atlas producer `ofChartsOfCompactSpace` (whose `CompactSpace` hypothesis is
28	  §2.1's genuinely a-posteriori one) becomes usable from a surjection.
29	
30	**What this is and is not.**  It is the plumbing of §2.2 steps 1, 2 and 4, discharged once.
31	Step 3 — surjectivity of the Abel map on points — is DJ-1's honest brick and is *not* proved
32	here.  Per §0.5 that brick must stay Challenge-free: use `exists_effective_of_picClass` /
33	`riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`.
34	
35	**AMENDMENT 2026-07-29, two corrections to the sentence this replaces.**  It used to say the
36	brick "needs the universal degree-`g` class, hence `divRep`, plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`
37	and the `fiberTwist` shift".  Both cost claims were wrong:
38	
39	* **Not `divRep`-gated.**  The effectivity content is landed and divRep-free at every point of
40	  any `Pic⁰`-representing object (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`,
41	  `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`).  Only the Abel *square* needs the
42	  representation.
43	* **No `fiberTwist` shift.**  At degree exactly `g` the entry condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)`
44	  reads `g ≤ deg W`, so the class sits on the boundary and `exists_effective_of_picClass` fires
45	  with no slack.  A shift is what one needs to lift a degree-*zero* class into the effective
46	  range, and that is one multiplication by a fixed degree-`g` class
47	  (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`), not a `fiberTwist` construction.
48	
49	What genuinely remains on this side is **descent**: the divisor is produced over a finite
50	separable splitting field of `κ(y)`, and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)`.
51	
52	Note that the statements below take the surjection as a *bare morphism* out of `DivScheme g`
53	rather than as an Abel map built from a representation.  That is deliberate: it keeps the
54	file independent of the divisor-representability chain, so the qc mechanism is available to
55	any producer of a surjection — including the chart-atlas route, which does not name an Abel
56	map at all.
57	-/
58	
59	set_option autoImplicit false
60	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
61	
62	universe u
63	
64	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
65	
66	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
67	
68	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
69	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
70	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
71	
72	/-! ## The qc step at the campaign's compact source -/
73	
74	section Qc
75	
76	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
77	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
78	variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
79	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
80	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
81	
82	/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step** (w4-datj §2.2 steps 1, 2, 4): if the Jacobian-to-be
83	receives a point-surjective morphism from the divisor scheme `DivScheme g`, its structure
84	morphism is quasi-compact.
85	
86	`DivScheme g` is a compact space (`compactSpace_divScheme`, DD-Q: it is a closed subscheme of
87	a Grassmannian pair with a finite affine atlas), the base `Spec k` is affine, and DJ-0's
88	`quasiCompact_of_surjective` converts a surjection out of a compact space into
89	quasi-compactness of the structure morphism.
90	
91	So the whole a-posteriori qc argument is reduced to surjectivity — which is DJ-1's honest
92	brick and is not supplied here. -/
93	theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
94	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
95	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
96	    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
97	  quasiCompact_of_surjective abel J.hom hsurj
98	
99	end Qc
100	
101	/-! ## DJ-2: the packaging -/
102	
103	section Package
104	
105	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
106	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
107	variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
108	variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
109	variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
110	
111	/-- **DJ-2, the packaging** (w4-datj §1.1): the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation
112	of the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
113	point-surjective morphism from `DivScheme g`.
114	
115	This is `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` with the fourth field replaced by the Abel-image
116	hypothesis, which is the form the classical construction produces: quasi-compactness of the
117	Jacobian is *not* structural (its atlas is infinite, §2.1) and has to come from the image
118	argument. -/
119	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelImage (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
120	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
121	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
122	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
123	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
124	    JacobianData C :=
125	  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft
126	    (quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel hsurj)
127	
128	@[simp]
129	lemma JacobianData.ofAbelImage_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
130	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
131	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
132	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
133	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
134	    (JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel hsurj).J = J :=
135	  rfl
136	
137	end Package
138	
139	/-! ## The chart-atlas form -/
140	
141	section Charts
142	
143	variable {ι : Type u} {Xc : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144	variable (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Xc i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
145	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
146	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
147	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
148	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
149	variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
150	variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
151	variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
152	
153	/-- **The atlas producer with the qc field discharged by the Abel image**: the infinite-atlas
154	producer `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` asks for `CompactSpace` of the glued object,
155	which §2.1 records as the genuinely a-posteriori input.  This supplies it from a surjection
156	out of `DivScheme g`, so an atlas plus a surjective Abel map is enough — no finiteness of the
157	chart index, which the chart index (one chart per divisor class with an effective witness)
158	does not have. -/
159	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage
160	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
161	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left)
162	    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
163	    JacobianData C :=
164	  JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft
165	    (compactSpace_of_surjective abel hsurj)
166	
167	end Charts
168	
169	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.JacobianDataAbelImage
7	
8	/-!
9	# DJ-1, the topological half: point surjectivity from residue-field lifts
10	
11	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` reduced DAT-J's quasi-compactness field to a single
12	statement, `Function.Surjective abel.base` — *step 3* of `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
13	§2.2, the node's one honest brick.  §2.3 describes the argument for it in the language the
14	Picard theory supplies: *every field point of `J.left` is a degree-zero class over its
15	residue field, shift it by `fiberTwist`, take an effective representative, and that
16	representative is a `DivScheme`-point hitting the original point.*
17	
18	That argument produces, for a point `y`, a **morphism** `Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g` — not an
19	element of the fibre of `abel.base` over `y`.  Nothing in the tree converted the first into
20	the second, and it is not bookkeeping that can be skipped: the target of DJ-1 is a statement
21	about the underlying *topological* map, while everything the Picard side produces is a
22	morphism of schemes.
23	
24	This file supplies exactly that conversion, and nothing else:
25	
26	> `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — if for every `y : Y` some
27	> `q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X` satisfies `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then
28	> `f.base` is surjective.
29	
30	The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
31	`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
32	so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
33	the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
34	*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
39	  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
41	  step from per-point lifts.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44	  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.
45	
46	## What this does NOT do
47	
48	It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49	`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50	§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
51	of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
52	instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
53	-/
54	
55	set_option autoImplicit false
56	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
57	
58	universe u
59	
60	open CategoryTheory Limits
61	
62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	/-! ## The conversion: per-point lifts give surjectivity -/
65	
66	section Topology
67	
68	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
69	
70	/-- **Per-point residue-field lifts give point surjectivity.**  If every point `y` of `Y`
71	admits a morphism `q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ X` with `q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y`, then the
72	underlying map of `f` is surjective.
73	
74	`Spec κ(y)` is nonempty (a field is nontrivial), and the range of `Y.fromSpecResidueField y`
75	is `{y}` (mathlib `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField`), so the image under `q` of any point
76	of `Spec κ(y)` lies in the fibre of `f` over `y`.
77	
78	This is the missing link between what the Picard side produces and what DAT-J's
79	quasi-compactness field consumes: `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields a *morphism* out of
80	a residue field, while `quasiCompact_of_surjective` wants a surjection of topological
81	spaces. -/
82	theorem surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift (f : X ⟶ Y)
83	    (h : ∀ y : Y, ∃ q : Spec (Y.residueField y) ⟶ X,
84	      q ≫ f = Y.fromSpecResidueField y) :
85	    Function.Surjective f.base := by
86	  intro y
87	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := h y
88	  -- a field is nontrivial, so `Spec κ(y)` has a point
89	  obtain ⟨s⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (Y.residueField y)))
90	  refine ⟨q.base s, ?_⟩
91	  have hs : (q ≫ f).base s = (Y.fromSpecResidueField y).base s := by rw [hq]
92	  rw [Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply] at hs
93	  exact hs
94	
95	end Topology
96	
97	/-! ## DJ-1's quasi-compactness step from per-point lifts -/
98	
99	section Qc
100	
101	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
102	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
103	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
104	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
106	variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
107	variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
108	variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
109	
110	/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step, from per-point lifts** (w4-datj §2.2 with step 3 in
111	the shape §2.3 delivers it): if every point of the Jacobian-to-be receives a
112	`DivScheme g`-valued lift of its residue-field point, the structure morphism is
113	quasi-compact.
114	
115	This composes `surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` with DJ-0's
116	`quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme`; the compact source is DD-Q's
117	`compactSpace_divScheme` instance, and the base is affine. -/
118	theorem quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme
119	    (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
120	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
121	    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
122	      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
123	      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
124	    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
125	  quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel
126	    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
127	
128	end Qc
129	
130	/-! ## The `JacobianData` producers -/
131	
132	section Package
133	
134	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
135	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
136	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
137	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
138	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
139	variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
140	variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
141	variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
142	
143	/-- **DJ-2 against per-point lifts**: the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation of
144	the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
145	`DivScheme g`-valued lift of every residue-field point of `J.left`.
146	
147	`JacobianData.ofAbelImage` asks for `Function.Surjective abel.base`; this asks for the
148	per-point lifts the classical argument produces, which is the same input one step earlier. -/
149	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelLifts (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
150	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
151	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
152	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
153	    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
154	      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
155	      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
156	    JacobianData C :=
157	  JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel
158	    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
159	
160	@[simp]
161	lemma JacobianData.ofAbelLifts_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
162	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
163	    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
164	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
165	    (hlift : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶
166	      DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
167	      q ≫ abel = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
168	    (JacobianData.ofAbelLifts C J rep hlft abel hlift).J = J :=
169	  rfl
170	
171	end Package
172	
173	/-! ## The chart-atlas form -/
174	
175	section Charts
176	
177	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
179	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
180	variable {ι : Type u} {Xc : ι → Scheme.{u}}
181	variable (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Xc i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
182	variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
183	variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
184	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
185	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
186	variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
187	variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
188	variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
189	
190	/-- **The atlas producer against per-point lifts** — the one critical-path §7.5 needs, since
191	the chart index is infinite and `CompactSpace` of the glued object is genuinely
192	a-posteriori.  Per-point residue-field lifts of the Abel morphism supply it. -/
193	noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts
194	    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
195	    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left)
196	    (hlift : ∀ y : (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left,
197	      ∃ q : Spec ((gluedOfCharts C f hf).left.residueField y) ⟶
198	        DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
199	        q ≫ abel = (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left.fromSpecResidueField y) :
200	    JacobianData C :=
201	  JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage C f hf hlft abel
202	    (surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift abel hlift)
203	
204	end Charts
205	
206	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# DAT-J's effectivity input at a **point of the representing object**
12	
13	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` produced an effective divisor of degree `g` from a
14	class of degree `g`, and its satisfiability face
15	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` does it from a class of degree **zero** plus a
16	fixed degree-`g` reference divisor.  This file walks that back one further step, to the datum
17	DAT-J actually holds: a **point of `J`** together with the `Pic⁰` universal property.
18	
19	## The chain, and where the divRep-gating actually starts
20	
21	A point `y : J.left` of the representing object of `pic0TypeFunctor C` gives, with no choices:
22	
23	1. the affine field test `Over.testPoint y : overSpec k κ(y) ⟶ J`
24	   (`Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean:176`) — mathlib's `fromSpecResidueField` read in the
25	   slice;
26	2. hence the restricted class `picEtMap C (testPoint y) λ` of any `λ : picEt C J`, and its
27	   fibre degree is `0` when `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C J` (`mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`);
28	3. a finite separable `L/κ(y)` and a presenting Čech class `M` over `L`
29	   (`exists_splitting_of_picEt`, `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean:143` — **unconditional** on the
30	   curve, which is what makes this file cheap);
31	4. `classDeg L M = 0` (`classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`,
32	   `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:98`);
33	5. and then this file's `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`: an **effective divisor
34	   of degree `g`** over `L` presenting `M · 𝒪(Z)`.
35	
36	**Nothing in 1–5 mentions the divisor-representability chain.**  So the "geometric half" of
37	DAT-J step 3 — the part `Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean` calls the honest Riemann–Roch
38	input `heff` — is *not* divRep-gated at all.  What *is* divRep-gated is the other half: that
39	the resulting `DivScheme`-point sits over `y`, i.e. the Abel-compatibility square, because
40	naming the Abel map at all requires the representation.
41	
42	## The honest limit, stated because it is easy to overclaim here
43	
44	The divisor produced below lives over the **splitting field `L`**, not over `κ(y)` itself, and
45	DAT-J's `hlift` wants a morphism out of `Spec κ(y)`.  Descending `L ↝ κ(y)` is a genuine
46	further step (finite separable descent — the `dat-g` lane's business), and this file does not
47	take it.  What it settles is that the effectivity content is available, unconditionally, at
48	every point of every `Pic⁰`-representing object.
49	
50	## TWO FURTHER LIMITS, from a fresh-context audit of this file (`I-0802`, `I-0800`)
51	
52	**(a) The reference divisor is quantified UNIFORMLY, which is strictly stronger than the
53	degree-`0` face asks.**  Because the splitting field `L` is produced *existentially inside the
54	proof*, the caller cannot name it in advance, so the hypothesis had to become
55	`Zof : ∀ L, (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor` together with `hZ : ∀ L, deg L (Zof L) = g` — a
56	degree-`g` divisor over **every** field extension at once, including `L = k`.  Compare the
57	single `Z` of `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`.  This has **no producer anywhere
58	in the tree**, and it is unsatisfiable exactly when the index of the curve does not divide `g`
59	(`deg` is residue-degree weighted, `RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean:61`).  It is the *binding* limit of
60	this file — stronger than the descent limit named above, which is the one the first draft
61	disclosed.
62	
63	**(b) A `PicRepDatum` face is NOT provided.**  The first draft of this docstring advertised
64	`PicRepDatum.exists_effective_deg_eq_at_point`, "the degree-zero class supplied by the universal
65	property rather than assumed".  **No such declaration exists** — it was never written, so the
66	one face that would consume the `Pic⁰` universal property is absent and `lam`/`hlam` remain
67	hypotheses the caller supplies.  Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because an advertised
68	declaration list is unchecked by any build.
69	
70	**(c) The cone is NOT `Challenge`-free**, and `w4-datj-worksheet.md` §0.5/§3.4 make that
71	binding for a DAT-J producer.  This file reaches `Challenge.lean` through
72	`Picard/DivisorDatumRankOne` → `Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance:6`.  Verified by reading the
73	import lines, not inferred.  §0.5's own claim that `FLVClass.lean` is Challenge-free is *also*
74	false at HEAD (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean:7` → `ChiCurve.lean` → `Challenge`), so the standing
75	"use `exists_effective_of_picClass`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`" rule no longer avoids the
76	cycle — both are downstream of `Challenge`.  That is a pre-existing tree-wide condition, not
77	something this file introduced, but it does mean the effectivity content is **not** yet
78	consumable by the planned DJ-2/DJ-3 discharge.
79	
80	## Main declarations
81	
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point` — from a degree-zero class on
83	  `J` and a point `y`, an effective degree-`g` divisor over a finite separable extension of
84	  `κ(y)`, presenting the shifted class.  Conditional on (a) above.
85	-/

94	
95	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
96	
97	open Scheme

99	noncomputable section
100	
101	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
102	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
103	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
104	
105	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftAbelEffectivePoint :
106	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
107	
108	-- The fibre-curve package at every field extension.  These do not synthesize through the
109	-- `relCurve` `def` barrier, so they are installed locally exactly as in
110	-- `Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivAssembleKappa.lean` and `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean`.
111	noncomputable local instance instIsIntegralRelCurvePt (L : Type u) [Field L]
112	    [Algebra k L] : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
113	
114	noncomputable local instance instSmoothRelCurvePt (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
115	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
116	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
117	
118	noncomputable local instance instQCRelCurvePt (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
119	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
120	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
121	
122	/-- **The effectivity input of DAT-J at a point of the representing object.**
123	
124	Given a degree-zero étale Picard class `lam` on a test object `J` and a point `y` of `J.left`,
125	there is a finite separable extension `L` of the residue field `κ(y)` and an **effective
126	divisor of degree `g`** on the fibre curve over `L` whose class is the restriction of `lam`
127	at `y`, shifted by a fixed degree-`g` reference class.
128	
129	Every step is a landed lemma and none of them is divRep-gated: `Over.testPoint` names the
130	field test at `y`, `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff` reads off `degAt = 0`, `exists_splitting_of_picEt`
131	(unconditional) presents the restricted class over a finite separable `L`,
132	`classDeg_presenting_eq_zero` reads the presenting class's degree as `0`, and
133	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` shifts by `𝒪(Z)` and produces the divisor.
134	
135	`Z` is the caller's degree-`g` reference divisor over `L` — in the campaign a multiple of
136	`fiberWeilDivisor`, whose degree is positive (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`). -/
137	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point (g : ℕ)
138	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
139	    {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C J) (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C J)
140	    (y : J.left)
141	    (Zof : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L], (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
142	    (hZ : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L],
143	      CurveDivisor.deg L (Zof L) = (g : ℤ)) :
144	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
145	        (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField y) L)
146	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField y) L)
147	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField y) L)
148	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField y) L)
149	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic) (E : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor),
150	      PicEtAff.map C L
151	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField y) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint y) lam))
152	            = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
153	        0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass L E = M * CurveDivisor.picClass L (Zof L) ∧
154	        CurveDivisor.deg L E = (g : ℤ) := by
155	  -- (3) the splitting of the restricted class at the field point of `y`
156	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M, hM⟩ :=
157	    exists_splitting_of_picEt C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint y) lam)
158	  letI := hLfield; letI := hkL; letI := hKL; letI := htow
159	  -- (2) the fibre degree of the restricted class vanishes, by membership of `pic0Subgroup`
160	  have hdeg0 : degAt lam (Over.testPoint y) = 0 :=
161	    mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam (Over.testPointField y) (Over.testPoint y)
162	  -- (4) hence the presenting class has degree zero
163	  have hM0 : classDeg L M = 0 :=
164	    classDeg_presenting_eq_zero C lam (Over.testPoint y) hdeg0 L M hM
165	  -- (5) the shift and the effectivity brick
166	  obtain ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl, hEdeg⟩ :=
167	    exists_effective_deg_eq_relCurve_of_classDeg_eq_zero g hχ L (Zof L) (hZ L) M hM0
168	  exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M, E, hM, hEeff, hEcl, hEdeg⟩
169	
170	end
171	
172	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# DAT-J step 3 is one compatibility square, not a construction
11	
12	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
13	`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift
14	
15	> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.
16	
17	The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
18	to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
19	is only that it sits over the right point.
20	
21	## What is landed, and had no consumer
22	
23	`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
24	chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:
25	
26	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
27	  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
28	  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
29	  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
30	  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
31	  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
32	  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
33	* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
34	  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
35	* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
36	  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
37	  (`:231`).
38	
39	This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
40	is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
41	hard does not exist fibrewise.
42	
43	## What is therefore actually missing
44	
45	`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
46	presenting `D`.  It says **nothing about `abel`**.  So joining it to `hlift` needs exactly
47	one statement — that classifying an effective divisor and then applying the Abel map
48	returns the class of that divisor's point:
49	
50	> `AbelCompatible abel` : for every field point and every effective degree-`g` divisor `D`
51	> over it, `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel` is the morphism `Spec K ⟶ J`
52	> named by the class of `D`.
53	
54	That is a *compatibility square*, not a surjectivity theorem, and it is the recorded
55	"groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (inbox `I-0525`): a bijection between divisor classes and
56	`DivScheme`-points is unusable until the square relating the two named morphisms lands.
57	
58	## Main declarations
59	
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square, as a named interface.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` — the square plus
62	  fibrewise effectivity gives the `hlift` obligation **verbatim** as
63	  `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` / `PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume it.
64	
65	## What this does NOT do
66	
67	It produces no `AbelClassifyCompatible` and no effectivity witness, so it builds no
68	`JacobianData`.  It removes the *construction* from DAT-J step 3 and leaves a square and
69	an effectivity input, both stated here rather than assumed anywhere.
70	
71	## AMENDMENT 2026-07-29: `heff` is NOT the divRep-gated half
72	
73	The text above calls `heff` "the honest geometric input", which is right, and the `dat-j`
74	roadmap row read that as work still gated behind divisor representability.  It is not:
75	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` and `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`
76	discharge the effectivity content, at every point of *any* `Pic⁰`-representing object, with
77	no `divFunctor`, no `DivFamZar`, no certificate and no chart
78	(`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`).
79	
80	So of the two halves this file separates, only the **square** is divRep-gated — naming
81	`abel` requires the representation.  They were never gated alike.  What the effectivity side
82	still owes is *descent*: its divisor lives over a finite separable splitting field of `κ(y)`,
83	and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)` itself.
84	-/

11	/-!
12	# The target degree is a WINDOW, not the genus — and at `deg = g` the two chart conditions coincide
13	
14	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` proves that a class of degree **exactly** `g` on a
15	curve with `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` has an effective representative of degree `g`, and its
16	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` docstring carries a retraction that ends:
17	
18	> "**So what this lemma does is RELOCATE the hypothesis, not discharge it** — `Z` is an
19	> argument. […] Producing `Z` is a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here."
20	
21	That retraction is **correct about `= g` and wrong about the obligation**, and this file
22	separates the two.  The arithmetic obstruction it records is real: `CurveDivisor.deg` is
23	weighted by residue degrees (`RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean`), so its image is `index · ℤ`, and on
24	a curve of index `3` and genus `1` there is no divisor of degree `1 = g`.  But that
25	obstruction is an artefact of the **equality**.  Read the proof of
26	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq`: the hypothesis `classDeg K L = g` is used twice, and
27	in one of the two places only `g ≤ classDeg K L` is needed —
28	
29	* to enter Riemann's inequality, via `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪) = deg W + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ deg W`;
30	* to *state* the conclusion's degree, which is where the equality is genuinely consumed.
31	
32	Decoupling them gives the same theorem over a **window** of target degrees, and then the
33	reference divisor is no longer an arithmetic hypothesis: the campaign's own
34	`m • fiberWeilDivisor π` has degree `m · δ` with `1 ≤ δ` (`deg_fiberWeilDivisor_windowδ`,
35	`one_le_windowδ`), so `g ≤ deg` is reachable at `m := g` on **every** curve, while `= g`
36	needs `δ ∣ g`.
37	
38	## The second half, and it is the one that changes another lane's plan
39	
40	At the *representability* degree `deg = g` the two conditions the chart layer treats as
41	separate are the **same condition**.  With `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g` the rank anchor
42	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) reads
43	
44	  `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = deg D + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1`,
45	
46	so **`h¹ = 0` alone forces `h⁰ = 1`** for a degree-`g` divisor.  `h¹ = 0` is what coverage
47	asks for (`IsSplitWitness`, and `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s drop-free membership);
48	`h⁰ = 1` is one of the four inputs of DAT-C GAP-2
49	(`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`).
50	
51	**SCOPED, 2026-07-29, by a fresh-context review of this file, before anything consumed it.**
52	A first draft of this paragraph said coverage's hypothesis and GAP-2's hypothesis are "the same
53	hypothesis", and that the index-slack residue and coverage's drop-freeness are "two faces of one
54	identity".  **Both sentences were too strong and are withdrawn.**  `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
55	takes **four** inputs — `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`, the class equation, and `h⁰ = 1` — and the identity
56	below substitutes only the last.  **Effectivity is passed through unchanged, and effectivity is
57	precisely what coverage does not carry**: `IsSplitWitness`'s own docstring
58	(`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:145-149`) says so, and warns in terms that apply exactly here that "a lane
59	that reads `IsSplitWitness` as already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one".
60	Dropping `0 ≤ D'` from the theorem below and closing with `exact?` fails.
61	
62	What survives, and it is worth having but smaller: **GAP-2 goes from four inputs to three** at
63	degree `g`.  Two further scopings of record, both from the same review:
64	
65	* the identity is *interderivable* with the already-landed `hb_forces_h0_eq_one`
66	  (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:180`, the same one-line proof), and `IndexSlack:175` already
67	  headlines "the χ-ledger turns it into an `h⁰` equality" — so the χ-ledger reading is not new
68	  here, only packaged;
69	* `IndexSlack`'s reading of its own conclusion as a defect concerns the *universally quantified*
70	  form ("**every** degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`", false with a moving degree-`g` family).  The
71	  pointwise form below is not a defect.  That distinction stands; the claim that it *unifies* the
72	  two findings does not.
73	
74	## Main declarations
75	
76	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg` — the window form: for **any**
77	  target degree `d` with `g ≤ d`, a class of degree `d` has an effective representative of
78	  degree `d`.  Strictly generalises `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq` (`d := g`).
79	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg` — the degree-zero face
80	  with the reference divisor's degree only **bounded below**, which is what removes the
81	  arithmetic hypothesis.
82	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` — and the reference divisor at that
83	  bound **exists on every curve of the campaign bundle**, so the face above is inhabited rather
84	  than conditional.  **It does NOT discharge the retraction's "open here"** — a first draft said
85	  it did, and that was withdrawn by a fresh-context review of this file: the conclusion weakened
86	  in lockstep with the hypothesis, so the divisibility obstruction moved from the *input* degree
87	  to the *output* degree rather than dissolving.  See the honest-limit paragraph on
88	  `exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_toP1`, and the review's own generalisation of the
89	  pattern (a weakened hypothesis can look like a discharged obstruction when it only relocated
90	  the same obstruction to the output).  The `π` in this statement is also **not load-bearing**:
91	  the section's `[LocallyOfFiniteType]` already gives `Scheme.residueDeg_pos`, so `d` copies of
92	  any non-generic point prove the identical conclusion with no `ℙ¹` anywhere.  `π` is kept
93	  because it is the datum the campaign's curve actually carries.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq` — the identity: at
95	  degree `g` with `χ = 1 − g`, `h¹ = 0` forces `h⁰ = 1`.
96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_eq_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` — GAP-2's
97	  uniqueness conclusion from the **coverage** hypothesis, with no `h⁰` input at all.
98	
99	## What this does NOT do
100	
101	It does not produce a chart, does not discharge `IsChartUniv`, and does not produce the
102	local-surjectivity instance.  It removes one arithmetic hypothesis from the effectivity leg
103	and identifies two chart-layer conditions at the representability degree.  The `V`-coupling
104	(I-0861, I-0869) and the `exists_factor` field are untouched and remain open.
105	-/

119	/-! ## The window form of the effective-representative theorem -/
120	
121	section Window
122	
123	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
124	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
125	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
126	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
127	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
128	
129	/-- **An effective representative at any target degree above the genus.**
130	
131	Identical in proof to `exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq`, whose `classDeg K L = g` is
132	weakened to a target degree `d` with `g ≤ d`.  The Riemann-inequality entry condition
133	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` reads `1 ≤ d + 1 − g`, i.e. `g ≤ d` — the equality `d = g` was only ever
134	the boundary case.  The degree conjunct still comes free from `deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq`.
135	
136	Taking `d := g` recovers the original statement, which is recorded as
137	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_of_window` below. -/
138	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg (g : ℕ) (d : ℤ)
139	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) (hgd : (g : ℤ) ≤ d)
140	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = d) :
141	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧
142	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = d := by
143	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K L
144	  have hdegW : CurveDivisor.deg K W = d := by
145	    rw [← classDeg_picClass K W, hW, hL]
146	  have hentry : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) := by
147	    rw [hdegW, hχ]; omega
148	  obtain ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_of_picClass W hentry
149	  exact ⟨E, hEeff, hEcl.trans hW, (deg_eq_deg_of_picClass_eq K hEcl).trans hdegW⟩
150	
151	/-- The landed `= g` statement is the `d := g` face of the window form — recorded so the
152	generalisation is visibly not a weakening. -/
153	theorem exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_of_window (g : ℕ)
154	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
155	    (L : X.CechPic) (hL : classDeg K L = (g : ℤ)) :
156	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L ∧
157	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = (g : ℤ) :=
158	  exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg K g (g : ℤ) hχ le_rfl L hL
159	
160	/-- **The degree-zero face with the reference divisor only bounded below** — the shape a
161	`Pic⁰` consumer meets, with the arithmetic hypothesis removed.
162	
163	`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero` asks for `deg Z = g`, and its own docstring
164	retracts that as "a genuine arithmetic hypothesis on the curve, open here" because `deg` is
165	residue-degree weighted.  Here `Z` need only satisfy `g ≤ deg Z`, which
166	`exists_reference_divisor_le_deg` supplies on every curve of the campaign bundle.  The
167	produced divisor has degree `deg Z` rather than `g`; that is the honest cost of the
168	weakening, and it is what the window form absorbs. -/
169	theorem exists_effective_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_le_deg (g : ℕ)
170	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
171	    (Z : X.CurveDivisor) (hZ : (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z)
172	    (L₀ : X.CechPic) (hL₀ : classDeg K L₀ = 0) :
173	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧
174	      CurveDivisor.picClass K E = L₀ * CurveDivisor.picClass K Z ∧
175	      CurveDivisor.deg K E = CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by
176	  refine exists_effective_deg_eq_of_le_classDeg K g _ hχ hZ _ ?_
177	  rw [classDeg_mul, hL₀, classDeg_picClass, zero_add]
178	
179	end Window

183	section Reference
184	
185	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
186	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
187	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
188	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
189	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

191	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

193	/-- **A divisor of degree at least `d`, on any curve carrying a finite dominant map to `ℙ¹`.**
194	
195	`d` copies of the fibre divisor: `deg (d • F) = d · deg F` (`deg_nsmul'`) and `1 ≤ deg F`
196	(`one_le_classDeg_fiberTwist_one` read through `classDeg_fiberTwist_one`).

200	weighted by residue degrees, so the image of `deg` is `index · ℤ`, and the campaign's own

202	of `δ` beyond `1 ≤ δ`, which is landed.

220	theorem exists_reference_divisor_le_deg (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π] [IsFinite π] (d : ℕ) :
221	    ∃ Z : Y.CurveDivisor, (d : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Z := by

249	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))

264	section RankAnchor

266	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
267	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral Y]
268	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
269	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
270	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

272	/-- **THE IDENTITY**: on a curve with `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`, a divisor of degree exactly `g` with
273	vanishing `H¹` has `h⁰ = 1`.
274	
275	One line from the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`: under `h¹ = 0`
276	the count is exactly `deg D + χ(𝒪)`, which at `deg D = g` is `g + (1 − g) = 1`.
277	
278	This is the coupling the chart layer treats as two conditions.  `IsSplitWitness` — hence
279	`chartLocus` membership, hence coverage — asks for `Subsingleton H¹`; DAT-C GAP-2 and the
280	chart map's injectivity ask for `h⁰ = 1`.  At the representability degree they are the same
281	ask, which is the structural reason `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean` could delete the greedy
282	drop rather than discharge it. -/
283	theorem h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_eq (g : ℕ)
284	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
285	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ))
286	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1)) :
287	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) = 1 := by
288	  have h := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) D h1
289	  rw [hdeg, hχ] at h
290	  omega

292	/-- **GAP-2's uniqueness from the COVERAGE hypothesis** — no `h⁰` input anywhere.
293	
294	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean`) is
295	DAT-C GAP-2: two effective divisors with the same class agree as soon as one of them has
296	`h⁰ = 1`.  The `h⁰ = 1` input is what `Pic0ChartPair.lean` calls the chart map's injectivity
297	obligation, and what `Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean` says membership does *not* need.

6:import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiCompact
7:import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UnderlyingMap
8:
9:/-!
10:# DJ-0: quasi-compactness from a compact-space source via a surjection
11:
12:The smallest, ungated brick of the DAT-J worksheet (`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
13:§2.4): the abstract topological shape that `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes to get
14:quasi-compactness of the Jacobian structure morphism from the Abel image of `Div^g`-lite.
15:
16:The mathematics is entirely mathlib's: the continuous surjective image of a compact space
17:is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). This file packages that for scheme
18:morphisms and adds the quasi-compactness corollary over an affine base, so DAT-J's qc
19:field is a one-line instantiation. It is deliberately **Challenge-free** (mathlib-only, no
20:curve/Challenge imports) — the DAT-J producer cone must not cycle through `Challenge.lean`
21:(worksheet §0.5 / risk 1).
22:
23:## Main results
24:
25:* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_surjective`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of
26:  schemes out of a compact-space source `X`, then `Y` is a compact space.
27:* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective`: a structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an
28:  affine base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives such a surjection. This is the
29:  shape DAT-J's DJ-1 consumes with `X := Div^g` (`compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel`
30:  the Abel morphism, `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`.
31:-/
32:
33:set_option autoImplicit false
34:
35:universe u
36:
37:open CategoryTheory
38:
39:namespace AlgebraicGeometry
40:
41:variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
42:
43:/-- **DJ-0, compact-image half.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of schemes out of a
44:compact-space source, then the target is a compact space: the underlying map of `f` is a
45:continuous surjection (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`), and the continuous surjective image of a
46:compact space is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). -/
47:theorem compactSpace_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X]
48:    (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : CompactSpace Y :=
49:  hf.compactSpace f.continuous
50:
51:/-- **DJ-0, quasi-compactness corollary.** A structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an affine
52:base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives a surjection `f : X ⟶ Y` from a
53:compact-space source `X`. Over an affine base, `QuasiCompact g` is exactly `CompactSpace Y`
54:(`HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine`, the `DivSchemeQProj` pattern), which the
55:compact-image half supplies.
56:
57:This is the abstract shape `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes: instantiate
58:`X := Div^g` (compact via `compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel` the Abel morphism
59:(surjective on points, DJ-1), `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`. -/
60:theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsAffine Z]
61:    [CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : QuasiCompact g :=
62:  haveI : CompactSpace Y := compactSpace_of_surjective f hf
63:  HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
64:
65:end AlgebraicGeometry

30:**What this is and is not.**  It is the plumbing of §2.2 steps 1, 2 and 4, discharged once.
31:Step 3 — surjectivity of the Abel map on points — is DJ-1's honest brick and is *not* proved
32:here.  Per §0.5 that brick must stay Challenge-free: use `exists_effective_of_picClass` /
33:`riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`.

35:**AMENDMENT 2026-07-29, two corrections to the sentence this replaces.**  It used to say the
36:brick "needs the universal degree-`g` class, hence `divRep`, plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`
37:and the `fiberTwist` shift".  Both cost claims were wrong:
38:
39:* **Not `divRep`-gated.**  The effectivity content is landed and divRep-free at every point of
40:  any `Pic⁰`-representing object (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`,
41:  `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`).  Only the Abel *square* needs the
42:  representation.
43:* **No `fiberTwist` shift.**  At degree exactly `g` the entry condition `1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)`
44:  reads `g ≤ deg W`, so the class sits on the boundary and `exists_effective_of_picClass` fires
45:  with no slack.  A shift is what one needs to lift a degree-*zero* class into the effective
46:  range, and that is one multiplication by a fixed degree-`g` class
47:  (`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero`), not a `fiberTwist` construction.
48:
49:What genuinely remains on this side is **descent**: the divisor is produced over a finite
50:separable splitting field of `κ(y)`, and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)`.
51:
52:Note that the statements below take the surjection as a *bare morphism* out of `DivScheme g`
53:rather than as an Abel map built from a representation.  That is deliberate: it keeps the
54:file independent of the divisor-representability chain, so the qc mechanism is available to
55:any producer of a surjection — including the chart-atlas route, which does not name an Abel
56:map at all.
57:-/

64:open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
65:
66:namespace AlgebraicGeometry
67:
68:variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
69:variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
70:variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
71:
72:/-! ## The qc step at the campaign's compact source -/
73:
74:section Qc
75:
76:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
77:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
78:variable (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (g r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
79:variable (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤))
80:variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
81:
82:/-- **DJ-1's quasi-compactness step** (w4-datj §2.2 steps 1, 2, 4): if the Jacobian-to-be
83:receives a point-surjective morphism from the divisor scheme `DivScheme g`, its structure
84:morphism is quasi-compact.
85:
86:`DivScheme g` is a compact space (`compactSpace_divScheme`, DD-Q: it is a closed subscheme of
87:a Grassmannian pair with a finite affine atlas), the base `Spec k` is affine, and DJ-0's
88:`quasiCompact_of_surjective` converts a surjection out of a compact space into
89:quasi-compactness of the structure morphism.
90:
91:So the whole a-posteriori qc argument is reduced to surjectivity — which is DJ-1's honest
92:brick and is not supplied here. -/
93:theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme (J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
94:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
95:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
96:    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
97:  quasiCompact_of_surjective abel J.hom hsurj
98:
99:end Qc
100:
101:/-! ## DJ-2: the packaging -/
102:
103:section Package
104:
105:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
106:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
107:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
108:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
109:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
110:
111:/-- **DJ-2, the packaging** (w4-datj §1.1): the pinned Jacobian datum from a representation
112:of the degree-zero Picard functor, its locally-of-finite-type certificate, and a
113:point-surjective morphism from `DivScheme g`.
114:
115:This is `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` with the fourth field replaced by the Abel-image
116:hypothesis, which is the form the classical construction produces: quasi-compactness of the
117:Jacobian is *not* structural (its atlas is infinite, §2.1) and has to come from the image
118:argument. -/
119:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofAbelImage (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
120:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
121:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
122:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
123:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
124:    JacobianData C :=
125:  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C J rep hlft
126:    (quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J abel hsurj)
127:
128:@[simp]
129:lemma JacobianData.ofAbelImage_J (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
130:    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
131:    (hlft : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom)
132:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J.left)
133:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
134:    (JacobianData.ofAbelImage C J rep hlft abel hsurj).J = J :=
135:  rfl
136:
137:end Package

139:/-! ## The chart-atlas form -/
140:
141:section Charts
142:
143:variable {ι : Type u} {Xc : ι → Scheme.{u}}
144:variable (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (Xc i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
145:variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
146:variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
147:variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
148:  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
149:variable {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {g r₁ r₂ : ℕ}
150:variable {b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k B ⊤)}
151:variable {b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)}
152:
153:/-- **The atlas producer with the qc field discharged by the Abel image**: the infinite-atlas
154:producer `JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace` asks for `CompactSpace` of the glued object,
155:which §2.1 records as the genuinely a-posteriori input.  This supplies it from a surjection
156:out of `DivScheme g`, so an atlas plus a surjective Abel map is enough — no finiteness of the
157:chart index, which the chart index (one chart per divisor class with an effective witness)
158:does not have. -/
159:noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage
160:    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
161:    (abel : DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ (gluedOfCharts C f hf).left)
162:    (hsurj : Function.Surjective abel.base) :
163:    JacobianData C :=
164:  JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft
165:    (compactSpace_of_surjective abel hsurj)
166:
167:end Charts

169:end AlgebraicGeometry

30:The proof is `Scheme.range_fromSpecResidueField` (mathlib): the range of
31:`Y.fromSpecResidueField y` is `{y}`, and `Spec κ(y)` is nonempty because `κ(y)` is a field,
32:so any point of `Spec κ(y)` maps into the fibre.  Composed with the DJ-0 lemmas this gives
33:the Jacobian datum producers in the shape the classical argument actually delivers: a
34:*per-point lift*, which is what `exists_effective_of_picClass` hands back.
35:
36:## Main declarations
37:
38:* `AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` — the conversion.
39:  Pure scheme topology; no curve, no Picard functor, no divisor scheme.
40:* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme` — DJ-1's qc
41:  step from per-point lifts.
42:* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` and
43:  `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelLifts` — the two `JacobianData` producers
44:  with the surjectivity hypothesis replaced by per-point lifts.
45:
46:## What this does NOT do
47:
48:It produces no lift.  Producing one is the divRep-gated mathematics of §2.3 (the
49:`fiberTwist` shift plus `exists_effective_of_picClass`, which must stay Challenge-free per
50:§0.5 — `riemann_inequality`, never `riemann_inequality_curve`).  What changes is the shape
51:of that obligation: a lift *per point*, stated with no reference to `Function.Surjective`,
52:instead of a global surjectivity claim about a topological map.
53:-/

56:set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
